Al-Mu'addal.question: The _____ was Saffarid ruler of Zarang in 911.
Al-Mu'addal.fact: Al-Mu'addal ibn Ali ibn al-Layth was the Saffarid ruler of Zarang for a part of 911. In 890 al-Mu'addal and his brother al-Layth helped their father 'Ali escape from imprisonment at the hands of the latter's uncle, the Saffarid amir Amr ibn al-Layth.

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mu'addal.question: Near the end of 908 al-Layth made a bid for power against 'Amr's son and successor Tahir by occupying part of _____
Al-Mu'addal.fact: Near the end of 908 al-Layth made a bid for power against 'Amr's son and successor Tahir by occupying part of Zarang.

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mu'addal.question: Al-_____ maintained his position, however, and Tahir was eventually forced to withdraw
Al-Mu'addal.fact: Near the end of 908 al-Layth made a bid for power against 'Amr's son and successor Tahir by occupying part of Zarang. Al-Mu'addal, who had been taken hostage by Tahir, was released in early 909 after Tahir was unable to dislodge al-Layth in an attempt to induce the latter to give up his struggle.

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mu'addal.question: Al-_____ was now amir, but many were opposed to him
Al-Mu'addal.fact: Near the end of 908 al-Layth made a bid for power against 'Amr's son and successor Tahir by occupying part of Zarang. Al-Mu'addal, who had been taken hostage by Tahir, was released in early 909 after Tahir was unable to dislodge al-Layth in an attempt to induce the latter to give up his struggle.

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mu'addal.question: He then moved on to _____ and killed a local leader there, but soon encountered stiff resistance and al-Layth was required to send him reinforcements
Al-Mu'addal.fact: He then moved on to Ghazna and killed a local leader there, but soon encountered stiff resistance and al-Layth was required to send him reinforcements.

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mu'addal.question: Despite this, he returned to _____ near the end of 909 having established the authority of al-Layth in the eastern provinces
Al-Mu'addal.fact: He then moved on to Ghazna and killed a local leader there, but soon encountered stiff resistance and al-Layth was required to send him reinforcements. Despite this, he returned to Sistan near the end of 909 having set up the authority of al-Layth in the eastern provinces.

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mu'addal.question: In Zarang, meanwhile, news of al-Layth's fall caused the people to recognize another brother, _____, as amir
Al-Mu'addal.fact: In Zarang, meanwhile, news of al-Layth's fall caused the people to recognize another brother, Muhammad, as amir. In an effort to cement his power, Muhammad imprisoned al-Mu'addal.

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mu'addal.question: Muhammad was subsequently forced to conduct a campaign against the _____ to the north
Al-Mu'addal.fact: Muhammad was subsequently forced to conduct a campaign against the Samanids to the north.

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mu'addal.question: This prompted him to negotiate with the _____, and at the end of July 911 he surrendered
Al-Mu'addal.fact: The Samanids arrived before the city in March 911 and initiated a siege. This prompted him to negotiate with the Samanids, and at the end of July 911 he surrendered.

Al-Mu'addal.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Mu'addal.question: His surrender allowed the _____ to take control of Sistan
Al-Mu'addal.fact: This prompted him to negotiate with the Samanids, and at the end of July 911 he surrendered. His surrender allowed the Samanids to take control of Sistan.

Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.question: The _____ was Companion of Muhammad and Muslim commander.
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.fact: Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya ibn al-Mughira ibn Abd Allah (Arabic: المهاجر بن أبي أمية المغيرة بن عبد الله, romanized: Al-Muhājir ibn Abī Umayya ibn al-Mughīra ibn ʿAbd Allāh) was a companion of the Islamic prophet Muhammad from the Banu Makhzum clan and a Muslim commander active in Yemen during the Ridda wars (632–633).

Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.question: Abu Umayya was well known for his generosity to traveling companions on the road and was popularly known as Zad al-Rakb (_____ for the Passengers)
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.fact: Abu Umayya was well known for his generosity to traveling companions on the road and was popularly called Zad al-Rakb (Provider for the Passengers).

Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.question: Al-Muhajir's sister was _____, one of the wives of Muhammad
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.fact: Al-Muhajir's sister was Umm Salama, one of the wives of Muhammad.

Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.question: He was a paternal first cousin of _____ ibn al-Walid

Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.fact: He married Asma bint al-Nu'man ibn Abi al-Jawn, a Kindite noblewoman and former wife of Muhammad; she later married al-Muhajir's Makhzumite kinsman Ikrima ibn Abi Jahl.

Al-Muhajir ibn Abi Umayya.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
